findings.title: Small-action flex conversion leaves action buttons off the right edge
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex row, but the old full-width float layout was removed without a flex replacement. Direct children are flex items, so float on them is ignored, and .small-action-desc stays at the initial flex: 0 1 auto (no flex-grow / flex: 1), so it shrink-wraps to its text instead of stretching across the row. The previous padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em, which made that block full width and kept text clear of the floated 45px avatar, was replaced with padding: 0 1.5%. The action button is still only float: right (line 309). If the button is a flex item, that float is ignored and there is no margin-left: auto, so it sits in source order next to the text. If it is nested in the description, the float still applies but only to the content-sized description box, not the post row. Either way undelete/delete/edit controls that used to pin to the right edge of the small-action row now sit immediately after short action text ("closed", "deleted", and similar). Browsers that ignore the new display values still honor float: left on .topic-avatar, and with the 4em offset gone the description overlaps the icon.

findings.title: Header panel is not pinned right under the legacy flex display values
findings.body: .panel lost float: right and is now pinned with margin-left: auto, while .d-header .contents is turned into a flex container by the new flexbox() mixin (and .title { float: left } was removed). Auto margins absorb free space only in modern flexbox. The mixin also emits display: -webkit-box and display: -ms-flexbox before display: flex, and those are the values IE10 and old WebKit actually keep, because they do not understand display: flex. In the 2009 box model and in IE10's 2012 flexbox, margin-left: auto does not consume free space, and float does not apply to flex/box items, so the removed float is not a fallback. Login, signup, notification, and user-menu controls therefore stay in source order immediately after the logo (and topic title) instead of at the right edge of the header — the browsers those prefixes were added to support. Pin the panel with a growing sibling (-webkit-box-flex: 1 and -ms-flex: 1) or the prefixed pack/justify properties, not auto margin alone.

findings.title: Header extra-info flex item can push controls off-screen
findings.body: order: 2 on .extra-info-wrapper only works if that element is a flex item of .d-header .contents, which is the new flex container, alongside .panel at order 3. As a flex item it keeps the default min-width: auto, so it will not shrink below its content's minimum size, and this change never sets min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, or flex: 1. .panel's margin-left: auto only moves the controls to the right when free space remains after items are sized. A long topic title (min-content is the longest unbreakable word, or the whole title if it cannot wrap) plus the logo and the icon panel overflows the header; the auto margin collapses to zero and the notification/user controls are pushed past the viewport or the page scrolls horizontally. Docked-header titles need min-width: 0 and ellipsis, or the row cannot shrink.

findings.title: order() mixin applies 0-based values to 1-based box-ordinal-group
findings.body: @mixin order copies $val unchanged into -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based and default to 1; modern order, -ms-flex-order, and -webkit-order are 0-based and default to 0. Legacy declarations must be $val + 1 (what Autoprefixer and Bourbon emit). As written, order(0) becomes ordinal-group 0 (invalid or sorted before every default item) and order(1) ties the item with every sibling that does not set an ordinal, whose default is already 1, so those items tie or swap in old WebKit/Firefox box layout while modern browsers keep the intended order. The current call sites pass 2 and 3, which still sort after the legacy default of 1, so this header does not mis-order today, but this mixin is the shared helper the PR adds and the first use of the normal values 0 or 1 will disagree across the browsers the prefixes exist for.

findings.title: align-items() mixin emits invalid and unmapped legacy values
findings.body: @mixin align-items forwards $alignment unchanged to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, and also emits -ms-align-items, which is not a real property (IE10/11 only implement -ms-flex-align). The 2009/2012 properties accept start and end, not flex-start and flex-end. @include align-items(flex-start) therefore produces a working unprefixed align-items: flex-start and legacy declarations those engines drop as invalid, so items fall back to the default stretch in the browsers this mixin is meant to cover. center and baseline, the only current call sites, happen to be valid in both syntaxes, so header and badge alignment are not broken by this today. Map flex-start to start and flex-end to end on the legacy properties only, and delete the -ms-align-items line.

findings.title: Header category bullet loses its vertical alignment offset
findings.body: The nested &.bullet { margin-top: 5px } rule under .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper was removed, and nothing replaces that offset. align-items: center on .d-header .contents only centers the whole extra-info wrapper against the logo and icons. The category bullet is still a float: left child of the wrapper (line 34), so its position relative to the topic title text is independent of the parent's flex alignment. line-height: 1.5 on the wrapper does not restore a 5px shift of the floated badge. The bullet in the docked header topic strip will sit about 5px higher than before relative to the title text.
